conventions.publishedAt/updatedAt: WordPress `date` / `modified`, i.e. the site's local (NZ) wall-clock, emitted verbatim as a quoted ISO-8601 string. NOT converted to UTC: several posts are published late evening NZ time and a UTC shift would move them to the next calendar day, changing the date the client publishes on.
conventions.excerpt: WordPress `excerpt.rendered`, tags removed and HTML entities decoded. Verbatim — auto-generated excerpts keep their WordPress '…' truncation and are flagged below rather than rewritten.
conventions.categories: Category NAMES resolved from the post's category IDs, in the order WordPress returned them. Includes 'Uncategorized' where WordPress recorded it.
conventions.attribution: Present only where the body carries a repost / original-reporting / original-segment line. `originalUrl` is copied byte-for-byte from the client's own link, tracking parameters included. The attribution line itself is also preserved verbatim in the Markdown body.
conventions.heroImage: WordPress featured media as {src, alt, width, height}, matching the existing `image` shape in src/data/schema.ts. Omitted where featured_media is 0.

globalDecisions: Elementor chrome removed: `data-elementor-*` container <div>s, `elementor-*` class attributes, inline styles, spacer widgets, and the tab/newline runs Elementor injects between widgets. Only the text, headings, lists, quotes, links and content images survive.

WordPress oEmbed cards (`<blockquote class="wp-embedded-content">` + a hidden `<iframe>`) were flattened to the plain Markdown link the blockquote already contained. The iframe is the visually-hidden preview; the link is its visible fallback, so no content is lost. These sit under the client's own 'Relevant articles of interest:' / 'Further Reading & Resources' headings — author-written cross-links, not a theme-generated related-posts widget, so they were kept.

Decorative 'Further Reading' section-logo images (Further-Reading-LOGO*.webp/.jpeg) were dropped on 3 posts: they are branded graphics sitting above the client's own 'Relevant articles of interest:' heading and carry no information the heading does not. Their WordPress alt text was the article's own title, not a caption. Listed per-article under `dropped` — restore if the client wants the graphic.
Adjacent <strong>/<strong> runs (WordPress splits words across tags, e.g. 'statutory dema' + 'nd') were merged so the Markdown renders as one bold run instead of literal asterisks.

Client typos and formatting quirks were NOT corrected: e.g. 'The short answer is , in most cases, no.' (can-ird-arrest-me-at-the-border-over-my-student-loan) and 'authored by Steve Kilgallon,.' (nz-student-loan-border-arrest) are verbatim from the source.
Verification: every post was re-checked by stripping all tags from the source HTML and diffing the word stream against the generated Markdown. Zero source words are missing from any of the 18 files.
